questions.q: On squared paper, Ravi draws a vertical blue line. He marks a dot 4 squares to the left of the line. Where must he mark a second dot so that the blue line is a line of symmetry of the two dots?
questions.a: 4 squares to the right of the line, in the same row
o: 4 squares to the right of the line, in the same row
4 squares to the right of the line, one row higher
8 squares to the right of the line, in the same row
4 squares to the left of the line, one row lower

questions.q: The chapter calls a flower, a butterfly and a rangoli symmetrical, but not a picture of clouds. What makes a figure symmetrical in the chapter's sense?
questions.a: some of its parts repeat in a definite pattern
o: some of its parts repeat in a definite pattern
it has exactly one line of symmetry
it is made only of straight lines
it is drawn in bright colours

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Every straight line drawn through the middle of a figure is a line of symmetry of that figure.
Reason (R): A line of symmetry cuts a figure into two parts that exactly overlap when the figure is folded along that line.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: (a) What is a line of symmetry of a figure? (b) Give one example of an object or figure from daily life that has a line of symmetry, and say where the line runs.
questions.a: (a) A line of symmetry is a line that cuts a figure into two parts that exactly overlap when the figure is folded along that line. (b) Any correct example, such as a butterfly, whose line of symmetry runs down the middle of its body, between its two wings.
s: (a) States that the two parts overlap exactly when the figure is folded along the line
(b) Gives a correct example and says where its line of symmetry runs

questions.q: On squared paper, a horizontal blue line is drawn. Dot P is 2 squares above the line and dot Q is 5 squares above it, in the same column. (a) Where must the mirror image of P be marked so that the blue line is a line of symmetry? (b) How many squares apart will the mirror images of P and Q be?
questions.a: (a) 2 squares below the blue line, in the same column as P. (b) The image of Q is 5 squares below the line, so the two images are 5 - 2 = 3 squares apart (the same gap as between P and Q).
s: (a) Places the image of P 2 squares below the line, in the same column
(b) Places the image of Q 5 squares below the line and finds the images 3 squares apart

questions.q: Answer each part in one line. (a) When a figure is folded along a line of symmetry, what happens to its two parts? (b) Does the picture of clouds at the start of the chapter have a line of symmetry? (c) When one half of a folded figure covers the other half completely, what are the two halves called?
questions.a: (a) The two parts overlap exactly; one covers the other completely. (b) No; no part of the clouds repeats in a definite pattern, so there is no line of symmetry. (c) Mirror halves.
s: (a) Says the two parts overlap exactly
(b) Says the clouds have no line of symmetry
(c) Names them mirror halves

questions.q:
Ananya is designing a border tile for her school's art room in Bhopal on squared paper. She draws a vertical blue line. On its left she colours 3 squares in the top row, 2 squares in the second row and 1 square in the third row, each time starting from the square that touches the blue line. She wants the blue line to be a line of symmetry of the finished tile. Each coloured square needs one sticker, and one sticker sheet has 15 stickers.
(a) In the top row, how many squares must she colour on the right of the line, and where?
(b) How many squares will be coloured on the finished tile?
(c) How many stickers will be left on the sheet after one tile?
(d) Can she make two such tiles from one sheet? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 3 squares in the top row, starting from the square that touches the line on its right side. (b) 6 squares on the left and their 6 mirror images on the right, so 12 squares. (c) 15 - 12 = 3 stickers are left. (d) No: two tiles need 2 x 12 = 24 stickers, but the sheet has only 15.
s: (a) Colours 3 squares on the right in the top row, starting next to the line
(b) Finds 12 coloured squares in all
(c) Finds 3 stickers left
(d) Says no, since two tiles need 24 stickers and there are only 15

questions.q: A craft teacher asks for three paper badges, each with at least one curved edge: one with exactly one line of symmetry, one with exactly two and one with exactly four. Meera suggests (i) a semicircle, that is, a circle cut in half along a diameter; (ii) a running-track shape, which is a rectangle 6 cm long and 2 cm wide with a semicircle joined to each of its two 2 cm sides; and (iii) a full circle. (a) Check suggestion (i). (b) Check suggestion (ii) and name its lines of symmetry. (c) Explain why suggestion (iii) does not meet the task. (d) Suggest a shape with curved edges that has exactly four lines of symmetry. (e) Name the four lines of symmetry of your shape.
questions.a: (a) A semicircle has exactly one line of symmetry, the line through the middle of its straight edge at right angles to it, so (i) works. (b) The running track has exactly two lines of symmetry, the line along its length through the middle and the line across its middle, so (ii) works. (c) Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry, so a circle has far more than four lines of symmetry; (iii) fails. (d) For example, a square with a semicircle joined to the outside of each of its four sides. (e) The vertical and horizontal lines through the middles of opposite sides of the square, and its two diagonals.
s: (a) Shows the semicircle has exactly one line of symmetry
(b) Shows the running track has exactly two and names them
(c) Explains that every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry, so it has more than four
(d) Gives a correct curved shape with exactly four lines of symmetry
(e) Names its four lines of symmetry correctly

questions.q:
Consider these statements about lines of symmetry.
I. Folding a figure along a line is one way to check whether the line is a line of symmetry.
II. The two parts on either side of a line of symmetry are mirror halves.
III. A line of symmetry of a figure is always either vertical or horizontal.
Which of these is or are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

Assertion (A): A rectangle that is not a square has fewer lines of symmetry than a square.
Reason (R): The diagonals of a rectangle that is not a square are not lines of symmetry, while both diagonals of a square are.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: True or False: A triangle with exactly two equal sides (the third side being different) has exactly one line of symmetry. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Its only line of symmetry runs from the corner where the two equal sides meet to the middle of the opposite side; folding along it makes the equal sides overlap, and no other fold makes the two parts match.
s: States True
Names the line from the corner between the equal sides to the middle of the opposite side as the only line

questions.q: Square EFGH has E at the top-left, F at the top-right, G at the bottom-right and H at the bottom-left. (a) Along which line of symmetry must it be reflected so that E and G stay in their own places? (b) In that reflection, which corner moves to the place where F was?
questions.a: (a) Along the diagonal joining E and G. (b) H moves to the place where F was, because F and H swap places.
s: (a) Names the diagonal joining E and G
(b) Says H moves to F's place as F and H swap

questions.q: Show that no triangle can have exactly two lines of symmetry.
questions.a: If a triangle has one line of symmetry, folding along it lays one side exactly on another, so two of its sides are equal. A second, different line of symmetry would make a different pair of sides equal. Then all three sides are equal, and a triangle with equal sides and equal angles has three lines of symmetry, one through each corner. So a triangle has 0, 1 or 3 lines of symmetry, never exactly 2.
s: Shows that one line of symmetry makes two sides equal
Shows that a second line makes another pair equal, so all three sides are equal
Concludes such a triangle has 3 lines, so exactly 2 is impossible

questions.q:
Match each figure in Column I with its number of lines of symmetry in Column II.
Column I: 1. Square  2. Triangle with equal sides and equal angles  3. Triangle with exactly two equal sides  4. Triangle with all three sides different
Column II: A. 0  B. 1  C. 3  D. 4

A hotel in Jaipur is setting tables for a wedding lunch for 120 guests. Each guest gets one cloth napkin folded once. The hotel has 70 square napkins (40 cm by 40 cm) and 80 rectangular napkins (40 cm by 30 cm). The planner wants every napkin folded into a triangle, with the two halves overlapping exactly.
(a) In how many different ways can a square napkin be folded once so that its two halves overlap exactly?
(b) Which of these folds give a triangle?
(c) If a rectangular napkin is folded into a triangle, will its two halves overlap exactly? Give a reason.
(d) Can every guest get a napkin folded as the planner wants? If not, how many guests need a different fold?
questions.a: (a) 4 ways: along the vertical middle line, the horizontal middle line and the two diagonals. (b) The 2 folds along the diagonals. (c) No; the diagonal of a rectangle that is not a square is not a line of symmetry, so the halves do not overlap exactly. (d) No: only the 70 square napkins can be folded into exactly matching triangles, so 120 - 70 = 50 guests need a different fold, for example a rectangular napkin folded along a middle line.
s: (a) Finds 4 folds: two middle lines and two diagonals
(b) Picks the two diagonal folds
(c) Says no, as a rectangle's diagonal is not a line of symmetry
(d) Decides no and finds 50 guests need a different fold

questions.q:
On squared paper, a vertical blue line and a horizontal blue line cross at point O. A red dot is 3 squares to the right of the vertical line and 2 squares above the horizontal line. Kavya must add red dots so that both blue lines become lines of symmetry of the pattern.
(a) Where is the mirror image of the red dot in the vertical line?
(b) Where is the mirror image of the red dot in the horizontal line?
(c) Where must the fourth dot go?
(d) How many red dots will the finished pattern have?
questions.a: (a) 3 squares to the left of the vertical line and 2 squares above the horizontal line. (b) 3 squares to the right of the vertical line and 2 squares below the horizontal line. (c) 3 squares to the left of the vertical line and 2 squares below the horizontal line. (d) 4 red dots.
s: (a) Places the image 3 squares left of the vertical line, 2 squares above
(b) Places the image 3 squares right, 2 squares below the horizontal line
(c) Places the fourth dot 3 squares left and 2 squares below
(d) Counts 4 dots in all

questions.q: Pooja folds a sheet of paper in half and opens it. She drops 3 separate blobs of paint on one half only, away from the fold, then presses the halves together and opens the sheet again. How many paint blobs does she now see?
A sheet is folded once. Arun cuts out a half-circle whose straight edge lies along the fold, cutting through both layers. What shape is the hole when the sheet is opened?
questions.a: a full circle

questions.a: a line of symmetry

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A square hole can be made at the centre of a square sheet with a single straight cut, if the sheet is first folded horizontally and then vertically.
Reason (R): After these two folds, the centre of the sheet lies at the closed corner of the folded paper, so a cut across that corner opens out into one hole in the middle.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Raj opens a square sheet that was folded once and punched once. He sees two holes at the same height, one 6 cm to the left of the vertical middle line of the sheet and one 6 cm to the right of it. (a) Along which line was the sheet folded? Give a reason. (b) If Raj folds the sheet along that line again, what will he see?
questions.a: (a) Along the vertical middle line, because the two holes from one punch are mirror images: at the same height and equally far (6 cm) on either side of it. (b) The two holes will lie exactly on top of each other.
s: (a) Names the vertical middle line, with the holes equally far on either side at the same height
(b) Says the two holes fall exactly on top of each other

questions.q: Answer each part in one line. (a) A square sheet is folded once and one hole is punched away from the fold. How many holes appear when it is opened? (b) A square sheet is folded vertically and then horizontally, and one hole is punched away from both folds. How many holes appear when it is opened? (c) In part (a), the hole was punched 5 cm from the fold, measured straight across. How far apart are the two holes on the opened sheet?
questions.a: (a) 2 holes. (b) 4 holes, one in each quarter. (c) Each hole is 5 cm from the fold, on opposite sides, so they are 10 cm apart.
s: (a) Gives 2 holes
(b) Gives 4 holes, one in each quarter
(c) Finds the holes 10 cm apart

questions.q:
Class 6B in Kochi is decorating the hall for Annual Day with punched paper doilies. Each square sheet is folded vertically and then horizontally, and Jaya makes 3 punches on every folded sheet, each punch away from both folds and away from the other punches. The class wants at least 100 holes in all.
(a) How many holes does one punch make on the opened sheet?
(b) How many holes will one sheet have?
(c) How many sheets are needed for at least 100 holes?
(d) Only 8 sheets are left. What is the smallest number of punches per folded sheet that still gives at least 100 holes?
questions.a: (a) 4 holes, one in each quarter. (b) 3 x 4 = 12 holes. (c) 8 sheets give 96 holes, which is too few, and 9 sheets give 108, so 9 sheets. (d) With p punches a sheet, 8 sheets give 8 x 4 x p = 32p holes; 3 punches give 96, too few, and 4 punches give 128, so 4 punches per sheet.
s: (a) Gives 4 holes per punch
(b) Finds 12 holes per sheet
(c) Finds 9 sheets, as 8 give only 96
(d) Finds 4 punches per sheet, as 3 give 96 and 4 give 128

questions.q:
Consider these statements about folded paper.
I. In the ink-blot activity, the fold becomes a line of symmetry of the pattern.
II. A sheet folded vertically and then horizontally, and punched once away from both folds, opens with 2 holes.
III. If a sheet folded once and punched once opens with only one hole, the punch was made on the fold.
Which of these is or are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: True or False: When a sheet of paper folded once is cut through both layers and then opened, the fold is a line of symmetry of the cut-out shape. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. The cut passes through both layers at once, so the part on one side of the fold is the exact mirror image of the part on the other side, and the two halves overlap exactly when folded back.
s: States True
Explains that cutting both layers together makes the two sides mirror halves across the fold

questions.q: A square sheet is folded along its vertical middle line and then along its horizontal middle line, then opened so that both creases are clear. Rohit refolds it the same way before each punch and opens it after each punch to count the new holes. Punch P is away from both creases. Punch Q is exactly on the vertical crease but away from the horizontal crease. Punch R is exactly on the horizontal crease but away from the vertical crease. Punch S is exactly where the two creases cross, at the centre of the sheet. (a) How many holes does P make? (b) How many holes does Q make, and where do they lie? (c) How many holes does R make? (d) How many holes does S make? (e) How many holes are on the sheet after all four punches?
questions.a: (a) 4 holes, one in each quarter. (b) 2 holes, both on the vertical crease, one above and one below the horizontal crease, because a hole on a fold is not doubled by that fold. (c) 2 holes, both on the horizontal crease, one to the left and one to the right of the vertical crease. (d) 1 hole, at the centre, since it lies on both folds. (e) 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9 holes.
s: (a) Gives 4 holes for P
(b) Gives 2 holes for Q, on the vertical crease above and below the centre
(c) Gives 2 holes for R, on the horizontal crease
(d) Gives 1 hole for S, at the centre
(e) Adds to 9 holes in all

questions.q: (a) What is an angle of symmetry of a figure? (b) Give one angle of symmetry of the paper windmill other than 360 degrees.
questions.a: (a) An angle through which a figure can be rotated about a fixed point so that it looks exactly the same as before. (b) Any one of 90 degrees, 180 degrees or 270 degrees.

(b) Gives 90, 180 or 270 degrees

questions.q: True or False: A figure that has a line of symmetry must also have rotational symmetry. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. A triangle with exactly two equal sides has one line of symmetry, but it looks the same only after a full turn of 360 degrees, so it has no rotational symmetry.
s: States False
Gives a figure with a line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry, such as a triangle with exactly two equal sides

questions.q: Nikhil says: 'If a figure does not look the same after a half turn of 180 degrees, it cannot have rotational symmetry at all.' Test his claim using a figure with 3 identical radial arms placed 120 degrees apart.
questions.a: Nikhil is wrong. The 3-arm figure looks the same after turns of 120, 240 and 360 degrees, so it has rotational symmetry. But 180 degrees is not one of these angles (180 is not a whole-number multiple of 120), so the figure does not look the same after a half turn. A figure can fail the half-turn test and still have rotational symmetry.
s: Lists the angles of symmetry 120, 240 and 360 degrees of the 3-arm figure
Shows that 180 degrees is not an angle of symmetry of it
Concludes the claim is wrong, since the figure still has rotational symmetry

questions.q:
A school in Lucknow is laying a corridor with square floor tiles. Three tile designs are offered. Design X looks the same after a quarter turn (90 degrees). Design Y looks the same after a half turn (180 degrees) but not after a quarter turn. Design Z looks the same only after a full turn. The tiler lays each group of 4 tiles in the four positions 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, one tile in each. A tile that does not look the same as in its starting position is lifted and re-laid the right way at Rs 10 a tile. X costs Rs 62 a tile, Y costs Rs 55 and Z costs Rs 50.
(a) Which design has no rotational symmetry?
(b) Write all the angles of symmetry of design Y.
(c) In one group of 4 tiles, how many tiles of each design must be re-laid?
(d) Counting the re-laying, which design is cheapest for a group of 4 tiles?
questions.a: (a) Design Z, because only a full turn of 360 degrees brings it back. (b) 180 and 360 degrees. (c) X: 0 tiles; Y: 2 tiles (the ones at 90 and 270 degrees); Z: 3 tiles (all except the one at 0 degrees). (d) X: 4 x 62 = Rs 248; Y: 4 x 55 + 2 x 10 = Rs 240; Z: 4 x 50 + 3 x 10 = Rs 230. Design Z is cheapest, even with the most re-laying.
s: (a) Names design Z
(b) Gives 180 and 360 degrees for Y
(c) Finds 0, 2 and 3 tiles to re-lay for X, Y and Z
(d) Finds Rs 248, Rs 240 and Rs 230 and picks Z

questions.q: Meena makes a badge by sticking a red paper windmill on top of a blue card design, with both centres on the same pin. The windmill looks the same after turns of 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees. Blue design P looks the same only after turns of 180 and 360 degrees. Blue design Q has 3 identical arms placed 120 degrees apart. The badge looks the same after a turn only if both the red part and the blue part do. (a) List the angles of symmetry of design Q. (b) Which angles of symmetry does the badge made with design P have? (c) Does that badge have rotational symmetry? Give a reason. (d) Does the badge made with design Q have rotational symmetry? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 120, 240 and 360 degrees. (b) Only the angles in both lists: 180 and 360 degrees. (c) Yes, because 180 degrees is an angle of symmetry strictly between 0 and 360 degrees. (d) No: the windmill's angles (90, 180, 270, 360) and design Q's angles (120, 240, 360) share only 360 degrees, so the badge looks the same only after a full turn.
s: (a) Lists 120, 240 and 360 degrees for design Q
(b) Finds the shared angles 180 and 360 degrees
(c) Says yes, as 180 degrees lies strictly between 0 and 360 degrees
(d) Says no, as the only shared angle is 360 degrees

Consider these statements.
I. If 36 degrees is the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure, then 90 degrees is also an angle of symmetry of it.
II. A figure with 8 identical radial arms at equal gaps has 8 angles of symmetry.
III. A whole number of degrees that is not a factor of 360 cannot be the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure.
Which of these is or are correct?
questions.a: II and III only

questions.q: A flower design has 18 identical petals at equal gaps around its centre. (a) Find its smallest angle of symmetry. (b) Write its order of rotational symmetry.
questions.a: (a) 360 / 18 = 20 degrees. (b) 18, since its angles of symmetry are 20, 40, 60, ... up to 360 degrees.
s: (a) Divides 360 by 18 to get 20 degrees
(b) Gives the order of rotational symmetry as 18

questions.q: True or False: A figure with 16 identical radial arms at equal gaps has a smallest angle of symmetry that is a whole number of degrees. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. Its smallest angle of symmetry is 360 / 16 = 22 1/2 degrees, which is not a whole number.
s: States False
Finds 360 / 16 = 22 1/2 degrees, not a whole number

questions.q: In a figure, 90 degrees is an angle of symmetry, and the figure has exactly two angles of symmetry that are less than 90 degrees. Find its smallest angle of symmetry and its order of rotational symmetry.
questions.a: The angles of symmetry are whole-number multiples of the smallest one. The two angles below 90 degrees are the smallest angle and twice it, so 90 degrees is three times the smallest angle. The smallest angle is 90 / 3 = 30 degrees. The angles of symmetry are 30, 60, 90, ... up to 360 degrees, that is 360 / 30 = 12 angles, so the order is 12.
s: Sees that 90 degrees is three times the smallest angle
Finds the smallest angle as 30 degrees
Finds the order of rotational symmetry as 12

questions.q: A rangoli has 12 identical petals placed at equal gaps around its centre. (a) Find its smallest angle of symmetry. (b) Write its next two angles of symmetry. (c) What is its largest angle of symmetry? (d) What is its order of rotational symmetry? (e) Will it look the same after a turn of 100 degrees? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. (b) 60 degrees and 90 degrees. (c) 360 degrees. (d) 12. (e) No, because 100 is not a whole-number multiple of 30.
s: (a) Finds 30 degrees
(b) Gives 60 and 90 degrees
(c) Gives 360 degrees
(d) Gives the order as 12
(e) Says no, as 100 is not a multiple of 30

questions.q:
A merry-go-round at a fair in Mysuru has 8 identical wooden horses placed at equal gaps around its centre. The owner plans to rebuild it with more identical horses, again at equal gaps. The fair committee asks that its smallest angle of symmetry be a whole number of degrees less than 40 degrees. The ride can hold at most 12 horses, and each new horse costs Rs 4,500.
(a) What is the smallest angle of symmetry of the ride now?
(b) Will the present ride look the same after a turn of 135 degrees? Give a reason.
(c) Which totals of horses from 9 to 12 meet the committee's rule?
(d) Which plan meets the rule at the lowest cost, and what does it cost?
questions.a: (a) 360 / 8 = 45 degrees. (b) Yes, because 135 = 3 x 45 is a whole-number multiple of 45. (c) 9 horses give 40 degrees (not less than 40); 10 give 36 degrees (meets the rule); 11 give 32 8/11 degrees (not a whole number); 12 give 30 degrees (meets the rule). So 10 or 12 horses. (d) 10 horses: add 2 new horses for 2 x 4,500 = Rs 9,000, cheaper than 4 new horses for 12.
s: (a) Finds 45 degrees
(b) Says yes, as 135 is 3 times 45
(c) Tests 9 to 12 and picks 10 and 12
(d) Chooses 10 horses at a cost of Rs 9,000

Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: A floor tile is a regular hexagon, with 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. (a) How many lines of symmetry does it have? (b) What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
questions.a: (a) 6 lines of symmetry. (b) It has 6 angles of symmetry, so the smallest is 360 / 6 = 60 degrees.
s: (a) Gives 6 lines of symmetry
(b) Finds the smallest angle as 60 degrees

questions.q: Gauri says: 'A regular polygon with more sides has more lines of symmetry. A circle has no sides at all, so it has no line of symmetry.' Check each part of her statement and give your verdict.
questions.a: Gauri is partly right. The first part is correct: a regular polygon with n equal sides has n lines of symmetry, so a regular hexagon (6) has more than a square (4). The second part is wrong: every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry, so a circle has endlessly many lines of symmetry, more than any regular polygon.
s: Accepts the first part with a reason (n equal sides give n lines of symmetry)
Rejects the second part: every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry
Gives the verdict that she is partly right

questions.q: Priya makes a cardboard model of the Ashoka Chakra with 24 identical spokes at equal gaps. (a) How many lines of symmetry does her model have? (b) What is its smallest angle of symmetry? (c) She removes every second spoke, so the spokes left are still at equal gaps. How many spokes are left, and what is the new smallest angle of symmetry? (d) She now wants a model whose smallest angle of symmetry is 45 degrees. Can she get it by removing more spokes from the model in (c)? Give a reason. (e) Can she get it from the original 24-spoke model instead? If so, which spokes should she keep?
questions.a: (a) 24. (b) 360 / 24 = 15 degrees. (c) 12 spokes are left, and the smallest angle becomes 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. (d) No: the spokes in (c) are 30 degrees apart, so any two of them are 30, 60, 90, ... degrees apart; 45 is not a multiple of 30, so no two spokes are 45 degrees apart. (e) Yes: the original spokes are 15 degrees apart and 45 = 3 x 15, so she keeps every third spoke, leaving 8 spokes.
s: (a) Gives 24 lines of symmetry
(b) Finds 15 degrees
(c) Finds 12 spokes and 30 degrees
(d) Says no, as 45 is not a multiple of 30
(e) Says yes, keeping every third spoke to leave 8

questions.q:
A jeweller in Jaipur cuts flat silver pendants shaped as regular polygons: a regular hexagon, a regular octagon (8 equal sides and angles) and a regular 12-sided polygon. Each pendant hangs on a pin through its centre and can be turned about it. A customer wants a pendant that looks exactly the same after a turn of 90 degrees and also after a turn of 120 degrees.
(a) How many lines of symmetry does the octagon pendant have?
(b) What is the smallest angle of symmetry of the hexagon pendant?
(c) Which of the three pendants look the same after a turn of 90 degrees?
(d) Which pendant should the jeweller offer the customer? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 8. (b) 360 / 6 = 60 degrees. (c) The octagon (smallest angle 45 degrees, and 90 = 2 x 45) and the 12-sided pendant (smallest angle 30 degrees, and 90 = 3 x 30); not the hexagon, as 90 is not a multiple of 60. (d) The 12-sided pendant: 120 = 4 x 30, so it matches after both turns, while the octagon fails at 120 degrees because 120 is not a multiple of 45.
s: (a) Gives 8 lines of symmetry
(b) Finds 60 degrees
(c) Picks the octagon and the 12-sided pendant
(d) Chooses the 12-sided pendant, as it alone also matches at 120 degrees

questions.q: Answer each part in one line. (a) How many lines of symmetry does a regular polygon with 7 equal sides and 7 equal angles have? (b) Name the figure for which every angle is an angle of symmetry. (c) How many lines of symmetry does the outer boundary of the new Parliament Building in Delhi have?
questions.a: (a) 7. (b) A circle. (c) 3.
s: (a) Gives 7
(b) Names the circle
(c) Gives 3

questions.q: True or False: A triangle with equal sides and equal angles has the same number of lines of symmetry as angles of symmetry. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. It has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side, and 3 angles of symmetry: 120, 240 and 360 degrees.
s: States True
Gives 3 lines of symmetry and 3 angles of symmetry (120, 240, 360 degrees)
